units.source: Understanding the source code of the different notes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Note source > Understanding the source code of the different notes

units.source: Internally, the structure of the content of each note is different based on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Types__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Note source > Understanding the source code of the different notes

units.source: For example:
units.context: Note source > Understanding the source code of the different notes

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes are represented internally as HTML, using the __TRILIUM_PH_2__CKEditor__TRILIUM_PH_3__ representation. Note that due to the custom plugins, some HTML elements are specific to Trilium only, for example the admonitions.
units.context: Note source > Understanding the source code of the different notes

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes are plain text and are represented internally as-is.
units.context: Note source > Understanding the source code of the different notes

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Geo Map__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes contain only minimal information (viewport, zoom) as a JSON.
units.context: Note source > Understanding the source code of the different notes

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes are represented as JSON, with Trilium's own information alongside with __TRILIUM_PH_2__Excalidraw__TRILIUM_PH_3__'s internal JSON representation format.
units.context: Note source > Understanding the source code of the different notes

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mind Map__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes are represented as JSON, with the internal format of __TRILIUM_PH_2__MindElixir__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Note source > Understanding the source code of the different notes

units.source: Note that some information is also stored as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_1__. For example __TRILIUM_PH_2__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_3__ notes use the attachments feature to store the custom libraries, and alongside with __TRILIUM_PH_4__Mind Map__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and other similar note types it stores an SVG representation of the content for use in other features such as including in other notes, shared notes, etc.
units.context: Note source > Understanding the source code of the different notes

units.source: Viewing the source code__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Note source > Viewing the source code

units.source: It is possible to view the source code of a note by pressing the contextual menu in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and selecting __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note source__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Note source > Viewing the source code

units.source: The source code will be displayed in a new tab.
units.context: Note source > Viewing the source code

units.source: For some note types, such as text notes and JSON notes, the source code is also formatted in order to be more easily readable.
units.context: Note source > Viewing the source code

units.source: Modifying the source code__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Note source > Modifying the source code

units.source: It is possible to modify the source code of a note directly, however not via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note source__TRILIUM_PH_1__ functionality.
units.context: Note source > Modifying the source code

units.source: To do so:
units.context: Note source > Modifying the source code

units.source: Change the note type from the real note type (e.g. Canvas, Geo Type) to Code (plain text) or the corresponding format such as JSON or HTML.
units.context: Note source > Modifying the source code

units.source: Confirm the warning about changing the note type.
units.context: Note source > Modifying the source code

units.source: The source code will appear, make the necessary modifications.
units.context: Note source > Modifying the source code

units.source: Change the note type back to the real note type.
units.context: Note source > Modifying the source code

units.source: Depending on the changes made, there is a risk that the note will not render properly. It's best to save a revision before making any big changes.
units.context: Note source > Modifying the source code

units.source: If the note does not render properly, modify the source code again or revert to a prior revision. Since the error handling for unexpected changes might not always be perfect, it be required to refresh the application.
units.context: Note source > Modifying the source code
